# NetSurf: standalone C libraries

This group contains libwapcaplet, libparserutils, libhubbub, libdom, libcss, libsvgtiny, libnsbmp and libnsgif. The browser application and any scripting engine are outside this group. Public headers and function inventory are described from `docs/core_catalog` at the project root. `SOURCE_ENTRIES.json` records the exact upstream revisions and MIT notices.

## Build

The parent collection enables this group. Standalone example:

```sh
cmake -S extensions/netsurf_extra -B build-netsurf -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=MinSizeRel
cmake --build build-netsurf
ctest --test-dir build-netsurf --output-on-failure
```

The standalone build requires an installed Expat development library. Inside the complete collection it uses the retained `LMX::expat` target. There are no downloads. Generated character/entity/gperf lookup tables and CSS property parsers are checked-in production C inputs, generated by the upstream Perl/gperf/C programs. Ordinary builds do not require those generator tools.

## C99 adjustments

Original vendor source bytes remain unchanged. `prepare_dom.cmake` removes file-scope semicolons following function-definition macros. `prepare_css.cmake` supplies the enum definition before use, replaces GNU union casts with C99 compound literals, and removes the unused tentative global `_ALIGNED` after the `css_rule` declaration, keeping the natural structure layout. `prepare_bmp.cmake` fixes bounds checks for ICO-contained DIBs, which do not carry the 14-byte standalone BMP file header. Every adjusted input is SHA-256 guarded and all changes are listed in `C99_ADJUSTMENTS.json`.

## Scope and ownership

HTML and XML are external document formats. CSS is a specialized document style language, not a replacement for LMX settings or execution. SVG produces paths, colours and text records; it does not provide a complete browser renderer. DOM includes Hubbub HTML and Expat XML bindings. The alternative libxml2 binding source is retained but not selected.

The code can be shared as independent immutable LMX data. Mutable C parser/document/string-interning state is separate: serialization and ownership policies belong in each L3 wrapper. In particular, shared immutable CODE references do not make the global libwapcaplet intern table thread-safe.

## Retention and validation

Production C/headers and generator inputs, license notices, concise READMEs, test code and example code are retained. CI/site files, screenshots, bulk image/XML corpora and downloaded archives are omitted. Some upstream tests refer to those external corpora or upstream test frameworks; their code is archival, while the six self-contained integration tests here run entirely offline and generate their own small inputs.

`COMPACTNESS.json` gives source payload sizes and static archive sizes; these are separate quantities. `VERIFICATION.json` records the original-tree and retained-tree builds, actual tests and archive comparison. Only Linux x86_64 execution was checked; portability on other targets requires their toolchains.
